s001.text: UPSC, twenty twenty-three. General Studies Paper Two, fifteen marks, two hundred and fifty words. Explain the constitutional perspectives of gender justice, with provisions and case laws. Here's the strange part. The same Article both bars and allows special treatment for women.

s002.text: Read what it asks. Explain means a clear account, no argument needed. And there are two named jobs: provisions, and case laws. We add two more. Statutes and figures. Then a balanced close.

s003.text: Start with the rule. Article fifteen one bars discrimination on grounds of sex. Article fifteen three allows special provision for women. Both stand together. That is the idea of substantive equality.

s004.text: The other provisions fill in the rest. Article fourteen, equality. Article twenty-one, dignity. Equal pay for equal work in Article thirty-nine. And one-third seats for women in Panchayats and Municipalities.

s005.text: But text needs courts to give it life. In nineteen ninety-seven, Vishaka laid down workplace guidelines because no law existed. Parliament passed the POSH Act in twenty thirteen.

s006.text: But cases moved further. In Joseph Shine, in twenty eighteen, section four ninety-seven fell. In Nitisha, in twenty twenty-one, indirect discrimination was recognised. Law moved from protection to autonomy.

s007.text: Now we write. Two hundred and fifty words, about eleven minutes. Open with Article fifteen. One line holds both the bar and the exception.

s008.text: Section one is the provisions, in five groups. Equality. Dignity. Directive Principles. The duty. And political participation.

s009.text: Section two is the case laws. Five cases, each with its year and its holding. Draw them as one timeline.

s010.text: Section three is the follow-through. The POSH Act. Maternity leave of twenty-six weeks. And women's labour participation, up from twenty-three point three to forty-one point seven per cent.

s011.text: Close with a balance, then see the easy answer. It treats Article fifteen three as unequal treatment. It says Mary Roy was an Article fourteen case. It is a ruling on succession law. It calls Vishaka the only law, and it names no cases.

s012.text: Here is the payoff. This frame answers its cousins. Twenty twenty-two asked about the right of movement. Twenty twenty-four asked about privacy and Article twenty-one. Learn the Articles once. The full story gets its own episode in our Polity series.
